paper.title_en: Tests of hadron calorimeter with cosmic muons at the MPD/NICA experiment
paper.abstract_en: The Multi-Purpose Detector (MPD) experiment at the NICA collider is designed to investigate the QCD phase diagram at high net baryon chemical potentials and moderate temperatures. The Forward Hadron Calorimeter (FHCal) is a key sub-detector dedicated to measuring the energy and spatial distributions of spectator nucleons, providing essential information on collision geometry, such as the reaction plane and centrality. The FHCal comprises two symmetric arms, each containing 44 modules with a lead-scintillator sandwich structure segmented into 7 longitudinal sections. To accurately determine the energy deposited by spectators, precise calibration of each FHCal module is required. This work presents the methods and experimental results of the FHCal calibration, trigger tuning and stability tests using cosmic rays. A procedure for reconstructing cosmic muon tracks is discussed, and an energy calibration method based on the measured track parameters and the corresponding energy deposition in each section is proposed. The results demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of cosmic ray calibration for the FHCal system prior to beam operation.
